findings.reason: the rule and the acceptance test are mutually unsatisfiable, so a node implementing the stated ordering fails the section's own gate while a node passing the gate implements a different ordering, and the starvation guarantee the section rests on has no mechanism behind it.
findings.text: §2 says admission orders across sessions "by priority first", with ageing applied only among equal priorities, and in the same breath says "the ageing rule still lifts any request that has waited past its bound, so a spent budget can move work ahead but cannot starve another session"; its own done-when at line 69 then requires a priority-0 request older than the ageing bound to be admitted ahead of a fresh priority-3 one

findings.reason: as declared §4 is dispatchable in parallel with §2 and its own done-when fails on priority and budget columns that do not yet exist.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires a queue view whose rows carry "its priority" and whose rows sit beside each session's budget, and both facts arrive only with §2; `<meta name="plan-section-depends-on">` declares only `s3 -> s2`

findings.reason: §4's scope is exposing an existing ordering and its reasons plus the genuinely new fields, not authoring the ordering; left as written a node may re-derive it, which the section's own requirement that the view and admission cannot disagree forbids.
findings.text: §1 states that no "importable function lists the queued and awaiting requests in the order admission will launch them, with the reason for each place", but `reckon.crew.queue_order.admission_order_details` already returns exactly that pairing, emitting "delivered review", "ageing", "priority override N", "roadmap priority" and "queued at (roadmap priority unavailable)"

findings.reason: a coordinator composing a node brief must name the log path, and a log left in a worker's scratch tree is not evidence a later reader can open.
findings.text: §2 and §3 delegate their gate log to "the section's evidence fragment" (line 82) without naming a path, and §4's done-when (line 96) names no evidence destination at all

findings.reason: the control is implementable as a mutation of the view's ordering, so it can fail and does show the guard fires; the base-revision form would be stronger but its absence does not invalidate the gate.
findings.text: §4's negative control is a stated counterfactual ("a view that ordered by queue time alone") rather than an arm run against the base revision, which is the form §2 and §3 use
